title: security parity: a cascade delete through the predicate-delete arm still refuses (and rolls back) on a child the caller may not delete — pins for #33699
body:
domain:server#5 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jRmmALkM1ftZxdVatQ

carries item 2 of #33699; #33699 keeps the engine change

Filing gate: ④ child of epic #33631 (SQL performance), split from #33699 by the maintainer's ruling 6893104201 (option B, 2026-11-15T10:39Z).

## What this card carries

The security-parity pins for #33699's cascade delete through the predicate-delete arm. Ruling 6893104201, point (2), verbatim: "a refused child rolls back the whole cascade, never skipped". Point (4): "record hooks still run per row".

Today (measured, os-dev-report 6892420600 at d7e1a5aa): every cascaded child runs the caller's by-id controlled-by-parent write gate (plugin-security) plus sharing `canDelete`. Any refusal rolls the whole cascade back. The predicate arm instead composes a row scope, and could skip an out-of-scope child silently.

## Expected

Pins in plugin-security / plugin-sharing test suites that hold on the engine change of #33699:
- a child the caller may not delete makes the whole cascade answer the same refusal as today, and no row (parent or child) is deleted;
- scoped matches that differ from the probed children refuse, never shrink;
- the audit, sharing-cleanup and file-reference hooks still run once per child.

Each pin is red against a deliberately skipping arm (ablation) and green against today's per-dependent path and #33699's change.

## Reader

domain:server#5 area A2 (S1). Serial with #33699 (A4, S2): the pins can land first against today's path, then guard #33699's PR. Size S–M.

## Dedupe

`repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue cascade predicate-delete parity` → only #33699 and epic #33631.
